    Code. - (1) New docs/guide/first_study.md, the user-guide page. Sections: - What you will compute: mean SAR in a 1 cm-radius gelled-saline sphere under an imposed uniform 1 V/m field at 64 MHz, checked against the closed form. - Before you start: the Docker service, complex mode source /usr/local/bin/dolfinx-complex-mode, and a cost of ≈ 5 min and ≈ 20 GiB summed RAM at 2 ranks (W2a: 282.4 s, 20.41 GiB, …W2a…:158). - The first study: the one tagged block. - Run it: save the block as a script and run mpiexec -n 2 python3 first_study.py inside the container in complex mode. - What you should see: one fenced ```text first-study-output block holding mean SAR = 8.0116577245e-08 W/kg. The prose says that the last digit or two can differ between runs (≈ 1e-11 relative) and that the test holds it to 1e-9. The closed form is 8.008354e-08 W/kg, 0.04 % away. - What this does not show: no coil, no ports, no h-convergence, an imposed field only. - How this page is tested: a relative link to the test module.

    The block uses only existing names and the Study defaults: no degree= and no density_kg_m3=. To reproduce GEOMETRY bitwise it writes R = 0.01 and resolution_sphere=R / 10, resolution_far=R / 5, the same float division as SPHERE_RADIUS / 10.0. It also passes GelledSalinePhantomMaterial(0.57, 78.0, 64e6), QuasiStaticSphereField(e0=1.0) and frequency_hz=64e6. It calls sar = study.mean_sar() and prints f"mean SAR = {sar['mean_sar_w_per_kg']:.10e} W/kg". It has no if __name__ guard requirement: the test execs with __name__ == "__main__", so either form runs. - (2) New tests/package/test_wf17_first_study_tutorial.py. - Helpers: - extract_tagged_block(text, tag) -> str. The opening fence is a line matching exactly ```python first-study (info string python <tag>, so GFM and mkdocs still highlight Python). The block runs to the next line that is exactly ```. Zero or more than one match raises LookupError. - exec_block(source, *, stop_before_solve) runs exec(compile(source, "docs/guide/first_study.md#first-study", "exec"), {"__name__": "__main__"}) under contextlib.redirect_stdout, and echoes the captured text from rank 0. Through pytest's monkeypatch, a spy wraps Study.mean_sar: it calls the original and records the instance and the returned dict. With stop_before_solve, Study.solve is replaced by a recorder that stores self and raises a private _StopBeforeSolve, which the helper catches. The spy never alters what the block computes. - Imports (names only, nothing restated): - GEOMETRY, _closed, MAT4_DEG1_RECORD from tests/package/test_wf15_study_lossy_sphere.py; - SIGMA_HIGH, EPSILON_R_SPHERE, FREQUENCY_HZ, E0, RHO_KG_M3 from tests/validation/test_lossy_sphere_sar.py; - MAT4_BAND (tests/materials/test_phantom_material_model.py:222); - L0_BAND (tests/validation/test_mat5_em_coupled_sphere.py:104); - run_checker and checker (tests/unit/test_doc_reference_exit_codes.py:46, :54); - complex_only (tests/complex_mode.py:26). - Every node prints the sha256 of the page bytes and of the extracted block. So, for chain U's re-run steps: - A record is (a) a value the node asserts by equality (== *_PRINT, string or list equality, rel 0), or (b) a named fixed-precision print of a physical quantity at 11 significant digits or fewer: a .4e / .6e / .10e value, a .4f list, a cell or dof count, a schedule string, a sha256. A record off its prior is BLOCKED, as the briefs say. - A reading is an identity residual (reciprocity, (U′), (Δ), (IT), (E), a node-JSON residual) or a distance-to-record (rel …, vs … record, (R) / (R4) / (R′)). So is any print finer than 11 significant digits that the node does not assert by equality: repr, .11e and finer, .12f near 1, hex (for example (c4)'s 8.291558128523365e-08, σ_max 0.999851545099, a .12e C_mode, S31's θ(P5) +1.224895450933e+00). Round-off at 1e-13 relative reaches their last digits. It is printed beside its prior and gated by its band only. When it moves inside its band, it is written in the Outcome and the slot continues: no known-issues entry, no 🟡. - One unit in the last printed place. A (b) record that moves by exactly one unit in its last printed digit, with its band green, is read as a rounding-boundary crossing. It is printed beside its prior, the slot continues, and the review reads it. Two or more units is BLOCKED. - A band red is BLOCKED, as before.

    The known-issues entries of items 938, 939 and 940 are retired by this ruling. WF-17's hold is lifted and the row returns to ✅. Items 943–945 run the windows the three items did not reach. Where a brief below this ruling lists a value as a record that this ruling classes as a reading, the ruling binds. The same goes for 941, 942 and 948, whose briefs predate it or were drafted beside it.

The three assertions of the weekly text: (B) python3 -m mkdocs build --strict exits 0 with zero WARNING lines; (P) the built site carries no path containing aed_results, COMPARISON_private or private/ (the docs/private tree, which builds to <site>/private/); (L) the site's text passes check_private_leak.py's digit scan against the raw AED exports.     PREDICTED RED: (B), and (P) on the tree as it stands. Mechanism, verified 2026-11-15: - (P) red as is. mkdocs.yml (25 lines) sets no docs_dir and no exclude_docs, so the docs directory is all of docs/. MkDocs copies every file under it into the site, whether or not the file is in nav. On this host docs/private/ holds the gitignored adjudication files (.gitignore:139–140; ls docs/private shows ten-plus files), and docs/references/ holds the operator-provided Jin text, both as markdown (jin-fem-3e/, .gitignore:128) and as an .epub. A plain build therefore publishes the private files and a copyrighted book. - (B) red as is. mkdocs is 1.6.1 in the image (measured: python3 -c "import mkdocs; print(mkdocs.__version__)" in the container prints 1.6.1; PyYAML 6.0.3). In 1.6, validation.links.not_found defaults to warn. docs/guide/ alone carries ≈1 540 relative links of the form ](../../src|scripts|tests|examples/…) that point outside docs/, and docs/ as a whole carries ≈1 545 ](../…) links (grep count, 2026-11-15). Each such link is a WARNING, so --strict aborts. What this step can do: fix (P) mechanically and measure (B).

    Negative control (asserted). The control runs in tmp_path on a synthetic docs tree, never on the repo: - (c-P): a scratch docs/ with index.md and private/x.md, plus a scratch mkdocs.yml without exclude_docs. Build it, and the (P) checker must find private/ in the site. Then add the repo's exclude_docs block, rebuild, and the checker must find nothing. - (c-L): one line holding a digit string generated at run time (secrets.randbelow, ≥ 10 digits, ≥ 5 distinct, never written to a tracked file), passed with {that string} as the secret set to check_private_leak.scan. It must return exactly one hit. Then the same scan over the real site lines with the real secret set. - (c-B): a scratch page linking ../outside.py under --strict must exit non-zero and print a WARNING line, which shows the warning counter can count.

    Traps. - Never build into site/ in the repo. Use --site-dir <tmp_path>/site. site/ is gitignored (.gitignore:47), but a built site holding private/ must never sit in the work tree, even an ignored one. - exclude_docs in 1.6 replaces the default exclusions. The default is .* and /templates/. Restate both in the block: .*, /templates/, private/, references/. Prove it with the (c-P) control, not by reading docs. - Excluding references/ is a privacy and copyright exclusion, not a nav choice. docs/references/README.md and birdcage-tuning-literature.md are tracked but go too: the whole directory is excluded so that the gitignored subtree can never slip through. - check_private_leak.py (scripts/testing/, 419 lines) has no scan-a-directory mode. Its CLI modes are staged, --message-file and --audit (:392–405). Import it by path (importlib.util.spec_from_file_location), and feed scan(lines, secrets) (:310–334) (relpath, lineno, text) triples from every text file in the site (.html, .js, .json, .xml, .txt; search/search_index.json holds the full text). Use secret_digits() (:190–194) without published_digits() subtraction (audit semantics: the site is a publication). Print hit locations only, never the token (:381–383); this output lands in a tracked log. - Count WARNING lines from the build's combined stdout+stderr (subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, text=True)), with the regex ^WARNING\b per line. In --strict, mkdocs 1.6 prints the warnings and then Aborted with N warnings in strict mode!. Record N and classify the first 20 by message type (link-not-found / nav / other).     Traps. - YAML 1.1 parses the bare key on: as boolean True under PyYAML 6.0.3 (in the image; docker/Dockerfile:15). Read the triggers as doc.get("on", doc.get(True)), and assert that exactly one of the two keys exists. Never quote on in the workflow just to please the test: GitHub accepts both forms, and the test must handle the canonical one. - "Installs only the docs extra" cannot be pip install ".[docs]". That installs the package itself and its core dependencies (pyproject.toml:25–39: fenics-dolfinx>=0.11.0,<0.12, petsc4py, slepc4py, gmsh, …), which are not pip-installable on an ubuntu-latest runner. Read the extra from pyproject.toml instead: python -c "import tomllib; print('\n'.join(tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb'))['project']['optional-dependencies']['docs']))" > docs-requirements.txt pip install -r docs-requirements.txt tomllib needs Python ≥ 3.11, so pin python-version: '3.11' or later. Test (I) as follows: - exactly one step runs pip install, and it is -r on the file generated from optional-dependencies']['docs']; - no other pip, conda or apt install step exists.
